Anima Magic is a type of magic born from the soul. Creatures rife with magic typically have one form of anima magic, if not more, and this is commonly shared across creatures within the same family, though some subfamilies are different enough to have unique ones to themselves. Even creatures that do not have souls, but a form of animating force, such as constructs, bear enough magic to have a kind of anima magic. For many of these creatures, use of this semi-anima magic is just another form of power they have in world where magic gives them life.

To those who can learn anima magic from others, such as chimerians, they need to be able to tap into the magic of other creatures’ souls and develop unique techniques or undergo profane transformations to reach into a new level of power. Their soul must be receptive and their own anima must be accepting to be able to acquire new power from another creature.

Anima spells have the Anima trait and require the caster to be able to perform them in the first place, typically through feats or features that unlock this capability, or innately if the anima spell is one their creature family has. They typically do not have a tradition and are focus spells. A creature must have focus points to cast anima spells. Being able to cast anima spell does not necessarily grant the ability to Cast a Spell like a spellcaster.

When playing with Anima Magic, creatures of specific families can have anima spells assigned to them. Depending on their level, they will have a number of focus points to be able to cast them, and some might have more than one anima spell. NPC creatures of level 1-8 will typically have 1 focus point and 1 anima spell, creatures of level 9-16 will have at least 2 focus points and 1 or 2 anima spells, while creatures of a higher level have 3 focus points and 1 to 3 anima spells.

Variant: Limited Anima Encounters

While anima magic is typically thematic and imparts a meaningful look at the natural place of magic in wild creatures and their lives, a GM might consider only allowing a single creature in an encounter to be able to cast their anima spells if it improves pacing and or make tactics interesting (such as a pack leader, or an elite variant). That said, for player characters that do depend on learning anima spells from creature encounters, such as chimerians, the GM is still encouraged to allow a chimerian to interact with any creature in the encounter to gain anima spells even if they are not built to use anima spells in combat.

Variant: Anima Pools

Another variation on how to play with anima magic is to use a separate pool of points, called anima points, to cast anima spells. This prevents a scenario where an anima spellcaster who has access to focus spells, or a spellcaster who uses focus spells that has access to anima spells to have less resource competition. Notably however, this does increase the versatility of a spellcaster who has access to both focus spells and anima spells, so a GM should plan accordingly. In this variation, any feature or activity that gains focus points can be used instead to gain anima points (such as refocusing or the Symbiosis actions for Chimerians), but not the other way around.

Variant: Anima Spells as Traditional Spells

As an alternative to treating Anima Spells as a unique focus-point based series of spells, it is possible to consider Anima Spells as traditional spells, either as a unique tradition of its own, or interspersed as Rare spells across all traditions with the Anima trait. In this instance, calls for Anima attacks or anima DCs will instead use Spell attacks and Spell DCs.

In this variant, anima spells require spell slots to cast instead of focus points. Classes that would use focus spells to cast Anima Spells instead gain spell slots to either prepare anima spells or spontaneously cast anima spells from. The list of anima spells provided are balanced with the presumption of them using limited, but renewable focus points instead of spell slots, so some of these spells may be weaker than their other peers.

Features that allow Anima-based characters to cast an anima spell without focus points, such as Chimerians with their Symbiosis actions could instead be altered to grant a free spell. This might lead to more spellcasting in a combat from these classes, so the GM should bear that in mind. Features that are dependent on the Chimerian effects of these spells when having them prepared or in a repertoire would behave similarly to if you had the anima spell ready for the day if they were focus spells.

If using a unique tradition, then these spells would unlikely be accessible to other spellcasters except those that cast spells from the Anima tradition. If the spells are interspersed across traditional spells, it is important that these spells have the Rare tag and have an access requirement for other spellcasters who may want to access them (though it may be prohibitive; especially if you are running a game where Anima magic is only accessible to those who have undergone specific training or procedures). The traditions the spells are assigned to are also important, generally tying certain families to traditions is one possible option. It is possible that a Primal spellcaster might have access to Beast Anima spells, while a Divine spellcaster might have access to Fiend Anima spells. Some families might also be multi-tradition, such as Undead spells being in the Divine and Occult lists.

Anima spells have the following template.

[Base Spell Rank] Name of the Spell (Number of Actions to cast)

Family The family the spell belongs to, and sub-family if relevant.

Anima Weapon Unarmed attack specific to the spell. Some features grant access to this weapon as an unarmed attack. If the anima spell calls for an anima strike, it uses this listed weapon for the spell attack.

Anima Morph Form size; General shape; Speeds. Some features allow transformations into a battle form granted by an anima spell, which would use these physical characteristics.

Anima Ability Some features allow one to benefit from the passive benefits listed on an anima spell. If the feature is an Apex feature, you can typically only benefit from one Apex feature at a time, chosen when you would benefit from more than one.

Traits Traits pertaining to the spell and its casting.

Requirements Any requirements necessary to cast the spell.

Trigger The trigger for the spell, if any.

Targets The targets for the spell.

Range The range of the spell.

Area The area of effect of the spell.

Duration The duration of the spell, if any.

Description of the spell.

(Heightened value) Effect of heightening.

Learning Anima Magic

To learn new anima magic, you must be able to interact with the soul to draw out its power. If you are a class or have a feature that grants you the ability to do so, you can take the Learn Anima Magic exploration activity.

Learn Anima Magic

 @Embed[Compendium.immortal-ardor.spells.f45Q8FGyQrpR7VDE inline hr=false]

Casting Anima Spells

Anima spells aren’t traditional spells, but they behave like focus spells in that they require focus points to cast and automatically heighten in rank with the character’s level.

Like spells, abilities that restrict you from casting spells (such as being polymorphed into a battle form) or protect against spells (such as a spell that protects against other spells or a creature’s bonus to saves against spells) also apply to anima spells.

When casting an anima spell, you must maintain at least one hand free as many of these spells typically involve some form of transformation or gesture to evoke and direct the release of anima magic.

Anima Attacks and DCs

When you cast an anima spell, some spells require attack rolls while some others require your targets to make a saving throw, much like regular spells would. For spells requiring targets to make a saving throw, they must roll against your Anima DC, which is equal to the highest of your class DC or spell DC unless specified. For spells requiring attack rolls, you need to make an Anima Attack Roll. Your anima attack roll uses the same proficiency and attribute modifier as your anima DC. Like a spell attack modifier, your anima attack rolls use the following formula: d20 roll + attribute modifier + proficiency bonus + other bonuses + penalties. This means your anima attack roll is typically 10 lower than your anima DC. A condition that reduces your attribute modifier’s value can reduce your anima attack rolls and anima DCs.

Some spells require you to make an Anima Strike with an Anima weapon. Anima weapons are considered unarmed attacks, and thus in these instances, you Strike with the spell’s anima weapon by making an anima attack roll or unarmed attack roll, whichever is higher, and you add Strength to the damage roll. Some features also grant you the anima weapon of a spell, which you can treat as an unarmed attack. Anima Strikes and granted anima weapons benefit from items that grant item bonuses to your unarmed attack rolls or increase your unarmed attack damage dice (such as fundamental runes on Handwraps of Mighty Blows). These items grant an item bonus to your anima attack roll, and if the damage die of the unarmed strike is lower, it gets increased to the amount listed on the item. Otherwise, items that grant item bonuses to spell attacks or DCs will grant their bonuses to your anima spells.

Notably, the base statistics of the anima weapon are also used in situations where a feature grants the weapon for use outside of the spell. Even if the spell heightens or alters the weapon statistic, these changes only take place when the anima spell is cast, unless otherwise noted.

Anima Transformations

Some anima features or options allow you to enter an Anima Transformation, where you turn into a creature listed on an anima spell, as listed in the spell’s Anima Morph entry. These features usually have the Polymorph trait, and for its listed duration you enter the battle form listed.

You gain the following statistics and abilities, some of which is dependent on the chosen anima spell block:

  • AC = Anima DC or 10 + Dexterity modifier + unarmored proficiency bonus + armor’s item bonus to AC, whichever is higher. Ignore your armor’s check penalty and Speed reduction.

  • Skill modifiers and proficiencies matching your existing skills.

  • You gain the trait that matches the creature family trait of your chosen spell.

  • You gain an anima weapon as an unarmed attack listed by the spell’s anima weapon entry. These attacks are based on your key attribute (for the purposes of conditions, for example). Your attack modifiers use your anima attack proficiency or unarmed attack proficiency, whichever is higher, and benefit from equipment or runes that improve your unarmed attacks or anima spells. Your damage bonus for these attacks is equal to your attribute modifier instead of Strength if it is higher.

  • Speeds based on the spell’s anima morph entry.

  • Additional features based on the spell’s anima ability entry.

  • While in this form, you can cast the anima spell affiliated with this transformation. Any frequencies, prerequisites or costs must still be met, but you can cast this spell once during this transformation without spending its cost (such as a focus point).

When a Dreamer or a dreaming entity leaves an imprint of themselves in Alamein, they give rise to a facet. In any given cycle where they could leave such a mark on the fabric of the greater dream, their ideas, their dreams, or their hopes could be given a formless shape of creativity. These imprinted ideas remain in Alamein from then on, thus existing in some form in every cycle and in any slice of Alamein, be it past, present, or future.

A facet is a concept or an idea given form; the idea of a spell, the concept of a powerful creature. Such things in the realm of creativity inspires, though it is rare that it actively persists. In fact, the creation of a facet is akin to how a Dreamer could conceive a Dreaming Entity, and for good reason – a dreaming entity is born from a Dreamer’s imagination, full of their passion and vision to the point where it is realized in the dream. Dreaming entities are full of these concepts and ideas – in other words, made up of multitudes of well-defined facets.

On their own however, a facet is a glimpse, a flash of color, or emotion, an idea that loosely floats in Alamein. They pool together and react with mana in strange ways that creates odd reflections or phenomena in the natural world. Such things are a mystery, but their effects are seen to those who look upon the night sky – a cornucopia of colors, stars, and nebulae. Some near, some far, and sometimes mistaken for other far-off stellar bodies in the distance. In some cases, these mana-facets are clumped in the air like a colorful smog, pool in beautiful crystalline puddles, or form luminescent cavern walls. Some facets are crystallized within solidified mana, found buried within the earth or having fallen from the sky.

To most denizens of Alamein, these are just magical occurrences in their world: a beautiful rock coated in mana-infused starstuff to create powerful tools, a gem of frozen mana to be turned into jewelry, or a fixture of wonderful manafalls, all adding to the beauty of their world or enrich their resources. Many of these mana-infused substances are used in some way or another in Alamein’s societies just like any other resource. VonArc Station famously uses a Mana Refractor Engine – utilizing a large Manastone reactor to power its entirety.

But these mana-infused resources bear facets, and these facets bear imprints, made up of the power of dreams. For those who can connect to these imprints locked within the facets, they can bring those powers to reality. In a budding and rare field of manacraft, select few who have the talent or undergo extensive training can channel the imprints within the facets.

Enter Somnistry.

Somnistry is one part theology, another part scientific magic that uses facets to call forth the power of Alamein’s constellations. It is the practice of using mana to channel the imprints out of a facet, giving rise to an element of creation born from the imaginations of the dreamer that created the facet in the first place. Those who practice somnistry are known as Asters, attaining the capability either via natural talent, extensive training, or through a life-changing event.

Those who believe in the theological elements of somnistry follow through on the ideas of the world being that of a dream, and each creature within it a dreamer that sleeps. A multilayered dream that flits in and out of consciousness, and that every entity is a part of a greater cosmos of stars that represent these dreams. While there are small groups and followings devoted to somnistry with their own tenets, deities, and faiths, it is not strictly necessary to adhere to any of these teachings, but some students find the metaphysical concepts helpful in their practice of somnistry.

To channel a facet’s imprints, an aster needs to first engrave the facet to their soul. Typically, facets can be drawn out from mana-infused matter and kept indefinitely within the aster. In many cases, mana crystals are suitable vessels that most asters carry or keep on hand, as they are portable and can contain facets that they would be able to channel. When engraving the facet, the aster pulls it out from the crystal, and keeps it within themselves as they channel its power. When they do not need it, or if they need to store it away for some reason, they can imbue it back into the crystal. Without the vessel to hold the facet, it could dissipate and be lost if the aster releases it from themselves.

No matter the accuracy of somnistry -influenced faiths, all dreaming entities are affiliated with a Constellation. This connection has meaningful implications for the properties of facets as well as the asters who channel them. Within a facet contains the imprints of the dreaming entity that created it, and these imprints are often locked multiple layers deep within the facet. Followers of somnistry hold that the facets and the imprints within are tied back to the constellations and stars the facet belongs to, and tapping to this connection is crucial to enable an aster to reach into these layers, dubbed asterisms.

Acquiring a Facet

A facet is typically first found embedded within a magical item or a mana-infused object. Any dreaming entity (a creature within Alamein) that is an aster could draw out the facet from this item if they can engrave it to their soul, and hold it within themselves. A creature can hold onto any number of facets without engraving them.

As the facets are held within the essence of the creature that carries them, they can’t be removed except on that creature’s death, or unless the creature releases it. Once released, it can either be engraved into a suitable vessel (typically a mana-infused object or mana crystal, such as the one the facet was originally found in) or transferred to another dreaming entity that can hold it. This can be done with a Crafting check with rules similar to transferring runes onto a runestone.

Facets can also be found lingering in points in Alamein that are dense with mana. If they can engrave it, they can draw this facet into themselves, otherwise they can engrave it to an appropriate vessel.

Engraving a Facet

A creature can engrave any number of facets they hold to their soul by attuning to it in a minute-long period of contemplation and focus. A creature can only engrave facets that have an item level that is of their level or higher and must meet any listed requirements to meet the benefit of the facet’s first asterism.

 

A Facet’s item block contains several important details:

  • The Type of Facet it is (Solar, Stardust, Vortex, or Nebula),

  • The Constellation they are affiliated with,

  • The Equipment associated with the facet,

  • The Powers granted by the facet’s imprints, and their respective Asterism levels.

 

If a creature has an attuned magical or biotechnical equipment that matches an engraved facet’s associated equipment, they can instead engrave the facet to the attuned item, and consider attunement for both items as taking a single attunement slot, instead. A piece of attuned equipment can only be bonded to a single facet unless described otherwise.

While the kind of benefit gained from binding to a facet differs by type, some facets grant stronger or additional benefits when it reaches new asterisms. A creature who can engrave a facet to themselves will gain access to at least the first asterism, but to reach new asterism levels they need to align themselves closer to the ideals and concepts of the facet. To do this, they first meet the requirements listed on the asterism level (usually a level, and sometimes a feat or other requirement).

 

Secondly, they need one or more of the following:

  • Align themselves with a Path of Somnistry, affiliating them with a particular type of facet,

  • Bridge themselves to the facet’s affiliated constellation, whether they are born under the same constellation, is sanctified under the constellation, belongs to a favored class of that constellation or to create some other bridge of their own,

  • Engrave the facet to its associated piece of equipment

 

Each of these requirements contribute to one increase in an engraved facet’s accessible asterism level, granting them the benefits and power offered by the new level.

 

Types of Facets

Facets are divided into 4 types: Solar, Vortex, Nebula, and Stardust. Each type corresponds to a type of benefit they provide to the creature that bonds to it, described in their individual sections below.

Casting a spell from a facet uses your class DC proficiency if it is higher than your innate spellcasting or your spell proficiency, and is cast at a rank that is equal to half your level rounded up. Using a feat from a facet that requires a class DC uses your class DC. Any granted feats or proficiency increases from a facet are considered temporary, and thus cannot be used for the purposes of meeting prerequisites, except if it is granted by another facet you have engraved.

All feats, spells, and other abilities granted by a Facet have the Constellation trait.

 

Solar Facet

Solar facets exemplify valor, and the most outward expression of a Dreamer. Solar facets give class feats. These class feats are usually affiliated with the Constellation or the Dreamer the facet belongs to.

Engraving these facets will grant the class feats to you even though you do not meet the prerequisites or are of a different class, unless the prerequisite feat or a class feature is necessary to perform any of the actions or gain benefits from the feat.

Stardust Facet

Stardust facets iconify wisdom, and a Dreamer’s innermost creativity. When you engrave a stardust facet, you are granted spells known as Constellation Spells. Constellation spells are a type of focus spell, requiring you to spend focus points to cast them, even if the spells the facets grant you are not typical focus spells.

You are granted a focus pool when you engrave to a stardust facet if you do not have one. Each stardust facet you engrave to grants you one focus point, up to a maximum of three.

Vortex Facet

Vortex facets represent courage, and in its inward motions lies a Dreamer’s will to shape their dreams.  Vortex facets grant you general and skill feats, as well as proficiency increases.

Typically, if you have the granted level of proficiency already, you will gain an extra benefit for engraving a vortex facet.

 

Nebula Facet

Nebula facets confer mysticism, and it reflects a Dreamer’s connection to the universe. Nebula facets grant a unique innate spell. These spells are incarnate spells, and you can cast only one nebula facet granted spell once per day, even if you engrave to another nebula facet.

Accessing higher levelled Asterisms on Nebula Facets allow you to cast the granted spell additional times per day, but this benefit is shared among all other nebula facet spells of that asterism. For example, if you have two nebula facets engraved and both have their second asterisms available, you can only cast the spell granted by one of the two facets a second time.
